newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan reaffirms commitment to peace with Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Sudan reaffirms commitment to peace with Uganda.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has said his country is committed to an Iranian initiative seeking to achieve peace between Sudan and Uganda.
The state television said Bashir made the statements during a meeting with Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Hossein Sheikholeslam on Saturday.
"Sudan is committed to the Iranian initiative to resolve the differences between us and Uganda through peaceful means," Bashir was quoted as saying.
Sheikholeslam told the television that he hoped to hold meetings next month with Ugandan officials in Kampala to try to settle differences between Sudan and its southern neighbour.
He handed Bashir a letter from Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on bilateral relations and the Iranian initiative, the television said.
Sheikholeslam also met Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha, it added.
Relations between Sudan and Uganda have been tense with each of them accusing the other of helping rebels attacking its territories. Both countries deny the charges.
Iran has been trying since last September to mediate between the two countries.
